messages:
Carla: multiple hosted customers reporting 500/503s and timeouts starting ~16:22 UTC. Support queue spiking, some customers also showing duplicate billing events after retries.
SRE_Bot: alert: surge in infer-runner exits (exit_code=137) and SIGSEGVs across us-west-2 between 16:20-16:35 UTC.
Alex Chen: tagging infra/runtime/support. Carla — can you paste a representative ticket + request_id?
Carla: Ticket C-1302: request_id=req_ab12; customer saw 503 at 16:24 then retried. Billing webhook later showed duplicate charge for same request. Snippet:
```
[16:24:09] api -> upstream 10.2.14.7 : 503 Service Unavailable
billing: webhook returned 200; charge_id=ch_dup_01 for req_ab12
```
Priya Nair: checking metrics: model=llama-13b-qk shows KV cache and host mem spike around incident window. Prefetch worker count doubled; memory peak ~+38% vs baseline.
Jonah Patel: grabbed pod logs for runner-4f2b:
```
[runner] FATAL: segmentation fault in attention_kernel
[runner] process 3194 terminated by signal 11
[container] restartCount=5
```
Mimi Walsh: need dmesg + kube events to determine OOM vs kernel fault.
Alex Chen: kubectl describe shows OOMKilled then restart. Node dmesg contains both OOM kill and segfault trace.
Jonah Patel: dmesg excerpt from node host-12:
```
[2026-03-17T16:23:58Z] Out of memory: Kill process 3194 (infer_runner) total-vm:5987328kB, anon-rss:4801200kB
[2026-03-17T16:24:01Z] segfault at 0 ip ... call trace: ...
```
Priya Nair: GPU NVML reported driver reset events ~same time. Could be driver reacting to bad GPU mem access or heavy pressure causing reset.
Carla: customers reported rising p99 latency before 503s; SDKs retried on timeout which apparently led to duplicate billing webhook deliveries — webhook handler doesn't dedupe on our request_id pattern.
Mimi Walsh: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) route a small percentage of traffic to a smaller quantized fallback, 2) disable KV prefetch for the model in region, 3) lower concurrency per GPU.
Alex Chen: do canary flow first. Mimi, set to 7% fallback and cap concurrency to 3 per GPU.
Mimi Walsh: canary active: model:llama-7b-quant receives 7% traffic in us-west-2; concurrency cap set to 3; KV prefetch disabled for llama-13b-qk.
SRE_Bot: routing change applied by Mimi at 16:40 UTC. Monitoring error rate.
Jonah Patel: reproducible steps for infra/runtime teams:
1) send sustained high-QPS (100+) long-context requests (seq_len >= 2500) to hosted endpoint
2) enable kv-prefetch=true and set batch_size large
3) observe host+GPU memory climb and container OOM within ~30-90s
Sample load test:
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 160); do curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{"input":"<very long context>"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate & done
```
Priya Nair: we'll spin an isolated node repro with heaptrack and nvprof overnight to capture allocator patterns and GPU traces. Also grabbing /var/log/nvidia for driver events.
Mimi Walsh: attached runtime backtrace for attention kernel:
```
#0 0x7f8d12bc in attention_forward
#1 0x7f8c9a01 in forward_pass
#2 0x55bbf3d0 in main_loop
```
Alex Chen: short-term: Carla, open billing ticket to add idempotency/dedupe on request_id for webhooks and reconcile dup charges. Communicate to affected customers.
Carla: opened BILL-365 with details: add request_id dedupe, idempotency_key support, and detection alert for duplicate charge events. Customer update drafted: routed to fallback, throttled, investigating; ETA 24-48h; issuing credits where we can validate duplicates.
SRE_Bot: error rate down ~68% after mitigations, although one node still shows intermittent segfaults at reduced QPS.
Mimi Walsh: temporary config changes applied: eviction_threshold bumped 0.80 -> 0.92 for affected pool; aggressive prefetch disabled for llama-13b-qk; fallback routing enabled until further notice.
Jonah Patel: hypothesized causes: 1) KV prefetch + long sequences exhaust host/GPU memory leading to OOM then kernel fault, 2) driver NVML reset bug under sustained pressure, 3) attention kernel edge-case triggered by low-memory quantization layout.
Priya Nair: next steps: collect coredumps where possible, run driver stress tests, try newer NV driver on single canary node, and validate runtime soft-limits.
Alex Chen: owners assigned: infra (Priya, Jonah) to root-cause driver/oom; runtime (Mimi) to add mem-headroom checks and soft caps; billing (Carla) to dedupe webhooks and reconcile charges. Follow-up sync scheduled 09:30 UTC tomorrow.
Carla: will keep this thread updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
